title: Two Beds, Ten Weeks
standfirst: Everything between today and first frost, ordered by how soon it stops being possible. The top block is the part with a closing window.

map.caption: Redrawn from your Figma plan and kept in your orientation, south at the top, so north points down. Grey blocks are the house, driveway, stairs and the townhomes. Fill shows how much sun each area gets: the more gold, the more sun. Unfilled areas are not yet surveyed.

beds.name: Path Bed
beds.aspect: South-east corner, out by the street
beds.description: Rosemary, sage and a big stand of shasta daisy, with bearded iris through the middle and a bare patch at the front. The herbs thriving here is the evidence for full sun and sharp drainage. This bed wants the opposite of a fall tidy: the woody herbs must not be cut back until spring.

beds.name: Street Bed Box 1
beds.description: The cut-flower box. Dahlias, gaillardia, scabiosa, cosmos and sunflowers, all still going. Needs constant deadheading for the next ten weeks.

beds.name: Street Bed Box 2
beds.description: Mostly finished and holding a lot of seed. One good clearing pass now, then it becomes the place hardy annuals get sown in September.

beds.name: Driveway Bed 1
beds.description: South-west corner of the property beyond the driveway, open to both the south and the west. On the plan this looks like it should get a lot of afternoon sun, possibly the most of any area outside the street boxes. Not seen yet.

beds.name: Front Lower Bed
beds.aspect: South side of the house, toward the street
beds.description: Between the house and the sidewalk on the south side, with nothing tall to its south. On the plan this is one of the two sunniest pieces of ground you own, and it is not even surveyed yet.

beds.name: Upper Lower Bed
beds.description: Directly against the south wall of the house, which is the prize spot on any property at this latitude. It collects sun all day and the wall radiates stored heat back at night, extending the season at both ends. It will also be the driest bed, sitting in the wall's rain shadow. If you want tomatoes, peppers, basil or figs, this is where they go. Worth surveying before anything else.

beds.name: Side Bed Box
beds.description: Narrow raised bed on the east wall of the house. Strawberries, beans on string trellis, sunflowers and the compost tumbler. East facing means sun through the morning and shade from around midday on, which is cooler than it looked. It also explains the mildew better than my earlier guess did: Seattle weather arrives from the south-west, so an east wall sits in a strong rain shadow, and the bed gets damp still morning air followed by no drying sun. That is close to ideal for powdery mildew. It is a fine spot for strawberries, a mediocre one for beans, and the wrong spot entirely for sunflowers.

beds.name: Driveway Bed 2
beds.description: West side alongside the house, beyond the driveway. Afternoon and evening sun is likely, subject to what stands on the neighbouring property to the west. Not seen yet.

beds.name: Back Bed 2
beds.aspect: West side of the house, north end
beds.description: Narrow bed on the west side of the house toward the north end, between the house and the stairs. Hemmed in, so worth watching rather than guessing. Not seen yet.

beds.name: Back Bed 1
beds.aspect: North-west corner, on the neighbour boundary
beds.description: The far north-west corner, up against the neighbouring property. Narrow, and north facing on a boundary, so likely shady. Not seen yet.

beds.name: Back Bed 3
beds.description: North wall of the house, and the shadiest ground on the property. The house sits directly to its south, so it is in shadow most of the day and effectively all day from October to March. The townhomes beyond it are further north still, so they take nothing from it. Plant it for shade and it will do fine; plant sun-lovers and they will always disappoint.

footnote: Ticking a box here is a local convenience for working at the bed. The durable record is content/plan.json. Frost timing is a ten-year average for in-city Seattle and varies by several weeks year to year, so treat November as a watch-the-forecast month rather than a dated one.
